provenance.title: Glute Bridge Causing Lower Back Pain?
provenance.creator: REACH Rehab + Chiropractic Performance Center
provenance.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (YouTube Creative Commons Attribution license)
provenance.excerpt: 44.2–52.5 s of original video. Cropped to the movement, muted, with instructional overlays excluded.

cases.note: At roughly 45.1 and 49.5–52.1 s in the source, hips keep rising past the neutral shoulder-to-knee line while the trunk visibly arches. Upper back stays supported. Grade for repeated overextension at top or a practical cue to stop at the straight body line. Do not grade generic lift-higher, pain, activation, or unsupported shoulders as correct.
